plate_comment: P0711 transmission fluid temperature sensor performance check (fault 298 = fault_detected_bits_288_to_303 bit 10 -> slot 127 -> P0711), run from cm848_periodicTaskGroup26_calibration8 (main-loop phases 1 and 21 of 40) when fuel_feature_control_flags bit 2 is set (EEPROM 0x170 = 0x11dc, set here). State 0 takes a start snapshot of the transmission, coolant and battery temperatures 40 passes after the engine reaches the governor setpoint, qualifies a cold soak (coolant under 9 deg F above the battery temperature, engine-off time 200 or more or unusable) and sets the too-hot flag when the transmission reads over 260 deg F with coolant and battery under 100 deg F (at or under it, and with the insufficient-rise flag clear, it clears P0711); with a start snapshot under 50 deg F it goes to state 1 above 30 mph out of park / neutral and tracks the sensor minimum and maximum. A swing of 16 deg F passes at once (state 5), still under 16 deg F after 12000 passes above 30 mph with the soak qualified sets the insufficient-rise flag (state 6); the verdict goes through cm848_updateTransmissionTemperatureSensorPerformanceFault and cm848_completeTransmissionTemperatureMonitorReport reports it (state 2 pass / 3 fail), state 4 = no verdict this key cycle: the check is disabled, or in state 0 a coolant (P0116 / P0117 / P0118), transmission (P0712 / P0713) or battery temperature (P0514 / P0516 / P0517) sensor fault, P0850 or an ECM fault (0 / 91 / 328 / 330 / 397) is set, or in state 1 P0500, P0712, P0713 or a start snapshot outside -35 to 260 deg F ends it, or the soak was not qualified at 12000 passes (was governorDataValidation).

plate_comment: Four wheel drive switch input task, run from cm848_periodicTaskGroup26_calibration8 (main-loop phases 1 and 21 of 40): the switch is a resistor ladder on ADC index 76, learned once the raw reading has been inside 54-563 counts after 600 warm-up passes (EEPROM-backed four_wheel_drive_switch_learned_flag_cal; until then the position code is forced to 1 and no fault is set). Once learned it runs the sensor channel pass every pass (cm848_processFourWheelDriveSwitchChannel, which also raises P0838 / P0839), debounces the decoded position code into four_wheel_drive_switch_position_code_debounced, forces the code to 0 when it changes between passes and sets fault 406 (P0837 = fault_detected_bits_400_to_415 bit 6, ROM 0x5985a[406] = slot 107) after 90 consecutive passes with a code of 0; any pass below that count clears it in the detected and registered words (was sensorValidationTimeout).
evidence: P0837 is not its whole job but the function is entirely the switch input handling, so the name covers the whole job. Disassembly confirms the flow: not learned -> sth 1 into slot 76 (@ 0x5228b8); learned -> bl 0x35ad0 channel pass, prev <- current <- slot 76 (@ 0x5228a0-0x5228ac); prev != current -> stable count 0 and slot 76 <- 0 (@ 0x522904-0x522910); persist count +1 only while slot 76 = 0 and learned (@ 0x52291c-0x522938); fault set at count >= 90 (@ 0x522950), else cleared (whole-file grep: the only clear of the 0xffbf mask). IDENTITY CAVEAT: the code alone proves a resistor-ladder switch with five valid windows (codes 1-5) and a learned-present latch; calling it the four wheel drive switch rests on the firmware's own P0837 / P0838 / P0839 mapping (faults 406 / 413 / 412) plus the table names four_wheel_drive_switch_position_code_*. Dump: learned flag 0, warm-up 600, slot 76 = 1, so on the dumped truck the monitor is unarmed. Timing: 90 passes about 9 s and 600 passes about 60 s at 100 ms per pass (5 ms per phase).

text: Lead 1 scope: the whole P0711 group is cm848_checkTransmissionTemperatureSensorPerformance (0x522b64) plus its verdict function, report function (cm848_completeTransmissionTemperatureMonitorReport, name already right) and initializer. Both EEPROM-backed result flag writers (0x522de0 / 0x522dfc / 0x522fd8 / 0x523024) and all three calls of the verdict function (0x522de4 / 0x522fe4 / 0x523028) sit inside the check function. Whole-file greps: the 298 clear mask 0xfbff is only in the verdict function and the start test, the 320 clear mask 0xfffe only in the P0720 monitor, the 406 clear mask 0xffbf only in the four wheel drive monitor (generic clear-all paths such as cm848_clearDiagnosticState / diag_resetAllFaults aside; they do not clear the two persisted P0711 flags).

Suggested enums (enums.csv, not a rename): transmission_temperature_rationality_state 0 QUALIFYING / 1 TRACKING_SWING / 2 REPORTED_PASS / 3 REPORTED_FAIL / 4 NO_VERDICT / 5 PASS_VERDICT / 6 FAIL_VERDICT; output_speed_sensor_check_state 0 NOT_TESTING / 1 TESTING / 2 HEALED / 3 FAILED / 4 DISABLED_BY_FAULTS.

cm848_periodicTaskGroup26_calibration8 (0x0000bd80, main-loop phases 1 and 21 of 40) runs four unrelated monitors (cm848_monitorOverboostAndHighLoadBoostBand, the four wheel drive switch, the P0711 check, the rail pressure sensor plausibility monitor): keep its name. cm848_phase_group_a_processing runs in the 20 even phases. cm848_resetTransmissionTemperatureValidation (0x3f6fc) belongs to the transmission temperature stability latch (substitution logic), not to the P0711 check: leave it.

P0711 enable: fuel_feature_control_flags (0x3fd5f2, EEPROM 0x170 = 0x11dc in the dump) bit 2 enables the check, so it is enabled in this calibration (the generic name and empty comment could say so). transmission_temperature_check_minimum_engine_off_time (0x408d56) is correct but could share the transmission_temperature_rationality_ prefix.

P0720 gate, do not read it as a calibration enable: bit 28 (0x10000000) of protection_feature_status_flags is pattern 28 of the condition matcher in cm848_calibration_group27_load (0x531900): bit n = (condition word & ROM mask[n]) == ROM expected[n] with 2-byte entries at 0x6430e / 0x6438e, here mask 0xc00a (@ 0x64346) and expected 0xc002 (@ 0x643c6). Reading the decompiled condition word (CONCAT11: high byte first) that means hpcr_battery_voltage_normal_flag and hpcr_battery_dwell_timeout_flag set, hpcr_governor_phase_active_flag set and fault 397 not registered - a runtime state. The RAM dump value 0x06ff4040 (bit 28 clear) is a key-on snapshot, so it says nothing about whether P0720 can run on the truck. The decode of the flag names is unverified; the monitor plate only says 'while bit 28 is set'.

struct field protection_condition_flags_t.threshold_current (byte at 0x40b0f0, offset 8) is a flags byte, not a threshold index. Bit 0x20 = P0720 output speed sensor fault: written only by the P0720 monitor (cpp 40043 / 40057), read by cm848_calculateTransmissionOutputSpeed (cpp 41222), cm848_learnOutputSpeedToVehicleSpeedRatio (cpp 34426) and cm848_updateTransmissionConditionFlags (cpp 33458). Bit 0x10 is written by cm848_processProtectionFaultSeverity (cpp 33829 / 33834, the store @ 0x34eac) and read in cm848_evaluateProtectionFaultCondition (cpp 33671); bits 1 and 4 are read in cm848_determineCurrentGearAndLockupInhibit (cpp 33420 / 33421). Rename the field and give it bitfields in structure_definitions.csv.

Type notes (no change proposed): 0x408d4a / 0x408d52 are typed word but loaded with lha (signed), as are the new rows 0x408d48 / 4c / 4e / 50 / 58 / 5c (i16); 0x3fd944 sensor_validation_timeout_cal is typed word but both readers use lbz (byte); governor-style state words 0x40b62a / 0x40b56e are read with lha and could be enum-typed.

Four wheel drive switch facts: ADC index 76 -> lookup (ROM 0x5ad50 axis / 0x5ad86 values) windows in raw counts: code 3 = 54-60, code 5 = 168-186, code 4 = 284-306, code 2 = 400-425, code 1 = 537-563, code 0 between windows, code 7 = 0-49 and 573-1023; channel config at 0x5ad40: default 1, high threshold 762, low threshold 11; the wrapper passes high_fault_bit 0x19c = fault 412 = P0839 and low_fault_bit 0x19d = fault 413 = P0838, so a raw reading above 762 counts sets P0839 and below 11 counts sets P0838 (sensorChannelTypeB_configInit sets high_fault_bit when the input is above high_threshold). Nothing reads the decoded code in this calibration (no absolute access to 0x40bb88 / 0x40be04 / 0x40b61a besides the monitor); the transfer case low range flag is computed from transmission_output_speed_in_use x 256 / vehicle speed (cm848_updateTransmissionConditionFlags), not from this switch. The code alone proves a five-window resistor ladder with a learned-present latch; the four wheel drive label comes from the P0837 / P0838 / P0839 mapping and the existing table names.

cm848_sciBuildStatusFlagsByte (0x51d5dc, plate 'bit meanings unknown'): its bits 0x40 = cruise_control_switches_learned_flag and 0x20 = four_wheel_drive_switch_learned_flag_cal are both learned-present latches reset by cm848_clearDiagnosticState inside the new-vehicle distance limit (32 miles here), so the byte is a learn status. cruise_control_switches_learned_flag (0x3fee00) sits in the EEPROM mirror (EEPROM 0x197e) but has no _cal.
